chunks: Abstinence is to shorten desires, to thank for bounties and to keep off prohibitions. If this is possible then (at least) the prohibitions should not overpower your patience; and do not forget gratitude when receiving blessings For Allāh has exhausted the excuses before you through clear, shining arguments and open, bright books.

key_terms.الزَّهَادَةُ: Abstinence or asceticism; detachment from worldly desires
key_terms.الْحَرَامُ: The forbidden; that which is haram
key_terms.الْحُجَجِ: The proofs; clear arguments or evidence
key_terms.الْكِتُبِ: The books; referring to scriptures or revealed texts
key_terms.الْمَحَارِمِ: The prohibitions; things forbidden by God
key_terms.الْوَرَعُ: Piety or caution; abstaining from prohibitions and doubtful matters
key_terms.صَبْرَكُمْ: Your patience; perseverance in the face of trials
key_terms.قِصَرُ الْأَمَلِ: Shortening of hope/desire; limiting one's expectations from the world

ai.seo_question: What are the three key virtues of Zuhd, Shukr, and Wara' in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) presents a triad of spiritual disciplines—zuhd, shukr, and wara'—grounded in the concept of 'qasr al-amal' (shortening hope), which counters worldly attachment by focusing on the Hereafter. This teaching emphasizes that despite clear divine proofs (hujaj musfira), human weakness requires conscious effort to prevent haram from overpowering patience (sabr). It reflects the Shia emphasis on balancing asceticism with active gratitude and vigilance against sin, supported by accessible scriptural evidence.
